newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary MKB boosts '96 profit, plans 12pct dividend.
newsitem.headline: Hungary MKB boosts '96 profit, plans 12pct dividend.

text.p: Hungary's Magyar Kulkereskedelmi Bank Rt (MKB) said on Thursday it expanded its business activity and profits in 1996 and planned to pay an unchanged 12 percent dividend to its shareholders.

"While we pursued an offensive expansion policies, we also did not forget about safety," CEO and Chairman Tamas Erdei told a news conference. He added that MKB boosted its pre-tax profit by 51 percent in 1996 to 9.22 billion forints from 6.1 billion forints in 1995.
He said that MKB, which is 58.2 percent owned by Germany's Bayerische Landesbank Girozentrale, planned to pay 12 percent dividend on its 1996 results.
The remaining profit would boost shareholders' capital to 30.4 billion forints from 23.9 billion, to create the source of further expansion, he added.

The bank said in a statement that the improvement in profitability covered the 16.7 percent increase in net interest income, the 69.3 percent rise in other operating income, as well as the decrease in operating expenses for three years, despite the continued expansion of branch network.
Between 1993 and 1996, MKB boosted its assets by 46 percent to 348 billion forints, increasing its customer loans by 63 percent and customer deposits by 45 percent, the bank said.

In 1996, the bank increased its market share in Hungary's corporate lending by two percent to 9.6 percent, while reduced its provision charge-to-loans ratio to one percent from 1.9 percent in 1996, the bank said.

Erdei said that MKB planned to increase its share in special project financing in Hungary as economic growth is seen picking up from this year, but most Hungarian companies still lacked capital for being good medium-term borrowers.
MKB said that its international banking relations were the most dynamically developing in central and eastern Europe in 1996, with the credits to foreign banks growing by 275 percent.
MKB managed to maintain its dominant position in payment services related to Hungary's foreign trade.

The bank plans to continue expansion in Hungary and in the region, where they plan to lead manage more syndicated loans in the future, encouraged by investment grades from Thomson BankWatch and IBCA, Erdei said.

He added the bank planned to increase its assets in 1997 at the same pace as last year, but the bank was not likely to boost its profits as rapidly due to increasing competition and falling interest rates in Hungary.
"If the profits are kept at the same level approximately, that is a good result," he added.
